title: Error terms for continued fractions of $e^{1/s}$ and $\sqrt{\frac{v}{u}}\tanh\!\Bigl(\frac{1}{\sqrt{uv}}\Bigr)$
summary: Many classical identities arise from nothing more mysterious than looking at the same object in two different ways. A number, a function, or a combinatorial object may admit several natural decompositions, and by disassembling it in one way and reassembling it in another, we often obtain unexpected corollaries. Telescoping sums provide a particularly vivid incarnation of this principle: by arranging terms so that successive contributions cancel, one performs a conceptual ``cut-and-paste'' that often admits a clean geometric interpretation.
